desc: Ideate the DP approach: backward DP with state (i, c, k) where k ∈ {1,2,3}, and reconstruction using greedy choice of smallest character that maintains global minimum cost.
Implement backward DP in Python within the Solution class, using array('i') for memory efficiency and the optimized transition with best array and min/second-min.
Compute global minimum cost as min over c of (|s[0]-c| + dp[1][c][1]), return "" if infinite.
Reconstruct the string by iterating i from 0 to n-1, trying characters c in 'a'..'z', checking if current_cost + |s[i]-c| + dp[i+1][c][new_k] == global_min, and updating state.
Test additional edge cases: n=1, n=2, n=3, all same characters, alternating characters, and a maximum length random string to ensure performance and correctness.
Verify memory usage is acceptable (array('i') uses ~4 bytes per entry, so ~16 MB for n=5e4).
